_about: HTA (medium voltage) in mainland France: the network tariff TURPE 7 HTA, 5 time slots with fixed pointe. Source: CRE deliberation 2025-78 of 13 March 2025 (TURPE 7 HTA-BT, in force 1 August 2025), pages 150-153. The grid operator sets the exact hours locally within the CRE rules; the hours below are the FR notebook's choice within those rules.

calendar.winter_note: saison haute: November to March by default
calendar.peak_hours_note: Sunday is entirely off-peak (heures creuses). Monday to Saturday have 8 off-peak hours set by the grid operator, here 22:00-06:00. CRE is moving off-peak hours from late 2025 to end 2027: summer favours 02:00-06:00 and 11:00-17:00 and avoids 07:00-10:00 and 18:00-23:00; winter avoids 07:00-11:00 and 17:00-21:00. A site's own hours go in its case overrides (tariff.calendar.peak_hours), as one peak window per weekday: off-peak hours split in two periods, or different in summer and winter, cannot be entered yet
calendar.pointe_note: fixed pointe: December to February, Monday to Saturday, 2 hours in the 08:00-12:00 window and 2 hours in the 17:00-21:00 window, the exact hours set by the grid operator (here 08-10 and 17-19)

regime_note: the TURPE option the site chooses for 12 months: LU long utilisation (the default, first) or CU short utilisation; choose CU in the case with regime {"auto": false, "manual": "CU"}

turpe_energy.note: TURPE 7 HTA pointe fixe, energy coefficients c1..c5: LU 2.65 / 2.10 / 1.47 / 0.92 / 0.68 c EUR/kWh, CU 5.74 / 4.23 / 1.99 / 1.01 / 0.69 (CRE 2025-78 p.151). Slots: pointe, HPH and HCH (winter peak and off-peak), HPB and HCB (summer)

turpe_cs.note: power component (CS): one subscribed power per slot, non-decreasing pointe <= HPH <= HCH <= HPB <= HCB, CS = b1 x P1 + sum b_i x (P_i - P_(i-1)) EUR/kW/yr (CRE 2025-78 p.150-151). The model subscribes exactly the metered peak of each slot. Fixed CG and CC are left out (the same with and without battery). Import above the contracted power is a hard limit (case grid.import_max_kw), so no CMDPS penalty
